chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about love and hatred, are they from faith? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And is faith anything but love and hatred?'
He made faith pleasing to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He made disbelief, transgression, and disobedience hateful to you; those are the rightly guided.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between love, hatred, and faith (Iman) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines faith (iman) not merely as belief but as a dynamic state of love (hubb) and hatred (bughd) aligned with divine will. By citing Surah al-Hujurat, he establishes that the internalization of faith involves both attraction to righteousness and repulsion from kufr and fisq, a concept central to Shia theological understanding of the heart's orientation. This narration underscores the affective dimension of faith, distinguishing it from mere intellectual assent.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the love and the hatred, are these from the Emān?’ So heasws said: ‘And is the Emān anything but the love and the hatred?’

Then heasws recited these Verses [49:7] but Allah has endeared the Eman to you and has Adorned it in your hearts, and He has made hateful to you the unbelief and transgression and disobedience; these it is that are the followers of a right way’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Fudayl ibnYasar who has said the following: “
I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Are love and hate part of belief?’ The Imam asked, ‘Is belief anything but love and hate?’

He then read the words of Allah, ‘. . . But Allah has endeared belief to you and has made it attractive to your hearts. He has made disbelief, evil deeds and disobedience hateful to you. Such people will have the right guidance.’” [49:7]
